english.title: Manslaughter
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) unlawfully killed **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..)
english.pointstoprove:

english.notes:
(i) The date of the offence is the actual date of death.
(ii) The rule that death must follow within a year and a day applies to acts or omissions before 16.9.96.
(iii) The rule is abolished for acts or omissions on or after that date which result in death. See Abolition - 'year and a day rule'
(iv) The consent of the Attorney General is required where: the injury was sustained more than three years before death; or the accused has been previously convicted of the offence alleged to be connected with the death.
(v) See also offence wording: H2097 re manslaughter - diminished responsibility/survivor of suicide pact.
(vi) Officers should carefully check an offender's previous convictions. Provisions under sections 224 to 235 of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 may mean that s/he is liable to receive a longer sentence if certain conditions apply.
(vii) The CPS have issued guidance for murder and manslaughter.
(viii) Where this offence is committed against an emergency worker, a life sentence is required unless there are exceptional circumstances; see the following sections of the Sentencing Act 2020: section 258A (detention for life - offenders under 18), section 274A (custody for life - offenders aged 18 - 20) and section 285A (life sentence - adults aged 21 or over); where these do not apply, the fact has to be treated as an aggravating factor in sentencing, see section 67 of that Act.
(ix) Terrorist connection - this offence is listed in Schedule 1 to the Sentencing Act 2020. Where the court has determined that there is a terrorist connection, the court has to treat this as an aggravating factor in sentencing (section 69 of that Act) and the notification requirements under the Counter-Terrorism Act 2008 apply (section 42 of that Act). In addition, section 23A of the Terrorism Act 2000 provides for forfeiture of money or other property.
(x) See section 72 of the Domestic Abuse Act 2021 regarding the committing of this offence outside the UK by a UK national or a person habitually resident in England and Wales.
